text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in the July 30 editions of Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Russian recruits into the military continue living in prison-like conditions, says Amnesty International.
- President Yeltsin during his holiday break seems to be putting in more time working than resting.
- A new managing director at the giant Krasnoyarsk aluminium smelter says he will not stay for long at the helm.
- Prominent international financier George Soros says he invested more than $980 million in Russian telecoms giant Svyazinvest.
- Separatist Chechen leaders have reacted strongly to Moscow's moves to alienate the rebel republic from major domestic communications lines.
- Opinion polls show that both civilians and servicemen agree that the Russian army is in dire need of reform.
- Russia urgently needs proper tax reform, says former Finance Minister Boris Fyodorov.
- The Interior Ministry will soon have to hand over its prisons and camps to the Justice Ministry.
- Russian business tycoons use announcers at TV stations they control to present themselves as the voices of public opinion.
- Moscow authorities have announced they will buy illegal firearms held by Muscovites at 'black market' prices.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais to work out a way to put an end to the scandal sparked by privatisation of telecoms giant Svyazinvest.
- Shares in Svyazinvest posted an unprecedented 10-14 percent rise within hours of the auction held to sell off a 25 percent stake in the company.
